title: Business overview
prompt: Explain what the company does, who pays it, and why the business exists. Cite primary sources.

title: Revenue model and segments
prompt: Describe revenue streams, segments, geographic exposure, pricing, and recurring versus transactional revenue. Date every mix figure.

title: Products and services
prompt: Describe the main products, customer problems solved, distribution, and product dependencies.

title: Customers and end markets
prompt: Describe buyers, use cases, concentration, contract duration, and end-market exposure. Do not infer undisclosed customer names.

title: Industry and value chain
prompt: Place the company among suppliers, distribution channels, customers, and substitutes. Explain cyclicality and supply constraints.

title: Competitive landscape
prompt: Identify direct competitors and alternatives. Compare specific products or business segments, with sources.

title: Moat and differentiation
prompt: Separate evidence from interpretation when assessing switching costs, cost advantages, intellectual property, scale, or network effects.

title: Growth drivers
prompt: Explain the mechanisms behind possible growth, their dependencies, and what would disprove them. Label forecasts and assumptions.

title: Financial performance
prompt: Record revenue, margins, earnings, cash flow, and relevant sector metrics. Every number needs period, units, currency, accounting basis, and source. Separate reported results, guidance, consensus, and estimates.

title: Balance sheet and capital allocation
prompt: Describe cash, debt, maturities, dilution, stock compensation, investment, acquisitions, dividends, and repurchases with dates and sources.

title: Management and governance
prompt: Describe leadership, ownership, incentives, governance, and execution history. Verify current roles and date the evidence.

title: Valuation context
prompt: Explain suitable valuation metrics and assumptions. Timestamp prices, share counts, net debt, and multiples; distinguish historical, current, and forward figures. Do not present an undated fair value.

title: Catalysts
prompt: List dated events, the mechanism by which they matter, uncertainty, and the next evidence to monitor. A scheduled event is not a guaranteed outcome.

title: Risks and thesis breakers
prompt: Describe operational, financial, regulatory, and competitive risks and measurable conditions that would invalidate an interpretation.

title: Scenarios and open questions
prompt: Separate bull, base, and bear assumptions from facts. Record missing data, disputed evidence, and research questions without inventing answers.

title: Relationships and themes
prompt: Link relevant companies and cross-sector themes. State the relationship type and supporting source; never imply all theme members are competitors.

title: Recent developments
prompt: Keep a dated, source-backed log of material changes. Distinguish the event date from the article date and explain what changed in the profile.

title: Sources and change log
prompt: List source IDs from the metadata and describe material research changes. Preserve conflicting or superseded evidence with dates and explanations.
